units.account: Col. Aubry holds the bridge as ordered. He lets the enemy column step onto it, then gives it volleys by battalion at under 200 m as it comes on, and keeps his line steady when the head of the column reaches the south end on his flank and the bayonets meet. The column is thrown back and he does not pursue over the bridge, as his order is to hold it, not to cross.

Col. Delacroix holds his line beside the 1st Battalion and gives fire on the bridge as ordered, pouring volleys into the flank of the column as it crosses. Cautious, he keeps his men in the line and does not follow the broken enemy.

Maj. Verneuil has no new order, but seeing the head of the enemy column stagger and break against the infantry on either side of the road he cannot sit still. He takes his squadron up between the two battalions, sabres the remnants at the south end of the bridge, and drives them back over it. He halts at the south end when he sees the enemy's second line on the far bank, and re-forms in the gap between the battalions.
units.departure: Projection sends the cavalry in pursuit over the bridge and up the road to (2000,348), killing most of the column (205+68+137 men). Verneuil is aggressive but sees a fresh enemy battalion lined on the far bank and enemy horse on the flank; he charges only to the bridge's south end, so he ends 1.2 km short of the projected position and the column loses far fewer men.

units.account: Col. Brandt takes his column at the double down the road and onto the bridge, with the bayonet and without halting to fire. Volleys from both battalions at close range cut it down on the bridge, and the head, reaching the far end, is caught by fire on both flanks and cannot take the position. The men turn about, the column breaks, and the survivors are driven back over the bridge by horse, the colonel with them.
units.departure: The projection kills 554 men and ends with the battalion at (1950,300). Here the column crosses the bridge as ordered and takes about 250 casualties from volleys during the crossing and at the far end, then another 100 from the sabres of the cavalry on the bridge, so it ends at 300 men (a difference of over 5% of its strength) and flees about 250 m in the time left rather than the projected 1 km.

units.account: Col. Hartmann moves his battalion down to the north bank and forms line on it as ordered. The enemy battalions are over 250 m off, beyond musket range across the river, so he does not waste his ammunition. He watches the Vanguard's column be repulsed at the bridge and holds the bank, shaken, awaiting orders.
units.departure: Projection leaves red-2 at (2250,1360), with morale 70. It forms on the bank at (2200,1390), which is within the tolerance, but the repulse of the column in front of it shakes it, so morale ends at 60.

units.account: Maj. von Reiter has no order and holds where he stands, watching the attack on the bridge fail. His men are uneasy after what they have seen.

summary: Red-1 stormed the bridge at the double in column, with the bayonet and without firing. Blue-1 and Blue-2, in line 70 m to either side of the south end, fired volleys into it from about the middle of the bridge onward and again at the far end. The column lost about 250 men on the crossing and at the south end, lost heart and broke, and the cavalry (Blue-3, acting without orders) cut down another hundred or so of the fugitives on the bridge and drove them back over it, ending at the south end. Red-1 ends at 300 men, broken, 250 m back on the north road. Red-2 lined the north bank but the Blue battalions were out of musket range across the river, so there was no fire. It lost some morale from the repulse. Red-3 held. Blue losses were light: about 15 men in each battalion and 3 in the cavalry. The bridge remains in Blue hands. The projection was too severe on Red-1 (554 killed) and has the cavalry riding up to the far end of the map; the umpire limited the pursuit to the bridge.
